verdict.reasoning: Patient reports dysuria and duration: 'It hurts when I pee.' and later 'Uh, six days.'

Patient states 'it hurts when I go to the loo, and I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out' and 'I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine... And is that just over the last, six days? Patient: Yes.'
Pain location, character, and severity: 'I've got, pain in my tummy.' 'In my lower tummy.' 'In the middle.' 'And how bad...?' 'Seven.' 'Comes and goes.'
Voiding and intake: 'have you actually been able to pass water OK? Patient: Yes' and 'have you been able to eat and drink OK? Patient: Yes.'
Absence of fever and back/loin pain: 'have you had a temperature?... Patient: No, not at all.' and 'you said you didn't have any lower back pain?... any loin pain as well. Patient: No.'
No discharge and regular periods: 'any other symptoms, any vaginal discharge or, anything like that? Patient: No, just the blood spot' and 'Do you have regular periods? Patient: Yes I do.'

No prior similar episodes and denies triggers: 'have you had these symptoms before? Patient: No. Doctor: Never. Patient: No.' and 'been doing lots of exercise, been dehydrated, um, been having regular sexual intercourse or anything? Patient: No.'
No weight loss or bowel change: 'Any change in your bowel habit? Any weight loss or anything? Patient: No. Patient: No.'
IBS history: 'Have you had any problems with your kidneys, or any urine infections? Patient: I had IBS before.'
Mebeverine dose and frequency: 'Do you take that regularly? Patient: Yes.' 'And it, do you take it three times a day? Patient: Yes I do.' 'Two hundred milligrams? Patient: Yes.'
Allergy: 'Any allergies? ... Patient: Clindamycin.' 'You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.'
Living situation and job: 'Do you live with friends, family? Patient: I live with friends.' and 'Where do you work? What's your job? Patient: I'm a support worker.'
Alcohol and smoking: 'Do you drink alcohol at all? Patient: Occasionally.' 'So how much in a average week? Patient: One glass of wine a week.' and 'And do you smoke? Patient: No.'
Doctor’s impression of UTI: 'it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine.' This is consistent with suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis in this context.
Transcript confirms IBS and mebeverine use but does not state IBS is 'stable' on mebeverine or discuss current IBS control.
Allergy documentation inference: 'Any allergies? ... Patient: Clindamycin.' 'You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.' This indicates a drug allergy to clindamycin is noted.
Empiric antibiotics and duration: 'we can treat this infection... with, with a course of antibiotics.' and 'It would just be for three days.'

Electronic prescription and timing: 'I can send a prescription through to your requested pharmacy for that.' and 'Can I just check that with you? Patient: Knightsbridge, Practice.' and 'the antibiotics, that I'm gonna prescribe, um, will go through to that, pharmacy.' 'How soon... In five minutes? Doctor: Um, I would give it longer than that. Give it a, an hour or so.'
Hydration advice: 'drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day.'
Cranberry juice: 'you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well, that sometimes helps.'
OTC urine-alkalinizing sachets: 'also some, sachets um, which you can get from the chemist, some sachets which just help change the acidity of your urine.'

Thermometer and monitoring: 'Have you got a thermometer at home? Patient: No.' 'It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature, just to make sure that it isn't, going up and down.'

Safety-net advice: 'if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again.'
